clue.text: Who'll have disturbed roosting? Loth, I

definitions.text: Who'll have disturbed roosting? Loth, I

indicators.note: something disturbed has been thrown out of its settled order, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to admit they spooked the birds on their perch.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a description: a bird-watcher is the sort who might disturb roosting birds, while the speaker is loth to own up.
explanation.definitionFit: A student of birds is the kind of person likely to get close enough to roosting birds to unsettle them.

clue.text: Oleander hand hooped with end of osier, twined

indicators.note: twined means twisted together, so the letters are wound into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of osier

explanation.surface: Describing a woven hoop of oleander bound with willow twigs.
explanation.walkthrough: An osier is a willow used for basketwork, which helps the picture of something twined.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhododaphne is an old name, from Greek 'rose-laurel', for the oleander shrub.

clue.text: Without extremes of cunning, such a situation is hopeless

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective that goes before 'situation' here

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, and without says they are dropped

parts.note: a knowing look is a cunning, shrewd one

explanation.surface: Without any wiliness at all, you are in a hopeless position.
explanation.walkthrough: Lose the outer K and G and NO-WIN is left; the definition is a phrase in which the answer fills a gap: a no-win situation is hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation is one where every outcome is bad, which is what hopeless means.

clue.text: Expert airman rising in foremost position, showing what's distinctive on wing tip

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the top is the leading place

indicators.note: in a down entry something rising reads from bottom to top, so the word is turned around

parts.note: an ace is a fighter pilot with many kills

explanation.surface: A star pilot climbing to the lead, with a mention of a wing tip to keep the aviation going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wing tip' looks like part of an aircraft, but a wingtip is a style of brogue shoe whose decorated toe piece is its signature.
explanation.definitionFit: A wingtip brogue is identified by its perforated, pointed cap over the front of the shoe.

clue.text: Religious schools (hard to find!) were on edge?

parts.note: were on, read as possessed one, the past tense of have plus the article
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Religious schools are scarce and their pupils on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'were on edge' as 'had a rim'. The bracketed aside is a wry note that the word is hard to find: Chambers lists it only under its singular, cheder.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadarim is the plural of heder (cheder), a Jewish elementary school teaching Hebrew and religion.

clue.text: Jock's daughter's bairn holds record in science

indicators.note: one thing holds another by having it inside

parts.note: oy is Scots for a grandchild, and Jock signals a Scottish word
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A Scottish grandchild who holds a record in science.
explanation.walkthrough: The daughter's bairn is the Scot's grandchild; bairn itself is Scots for child.
explanation.definitionFit: An ology is a jocular word for any branch of learning, taken from names like biology.

clue.text: Pair of stipules wild sorrel has on inside

indicators.note: having something inside means wrapping around it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: oca is a South American wood sorrel
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A botanical note on the leaf-base parts of a wild sorrel.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocrea is a sheath round a stem formed by two stipules joined together, as in the dock family.

clue.text: One in automatic maybe making progress in Scotland

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: an automatic is a kind of firearm, hence maybe
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone driving an automatic car making headway in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Automatic' suggests a car; here it is a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaun is the Scots form of going, as in moving forward or getting on.

clue.text: I'm pressing about sort of weed that's coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry something coming up reads from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: re means about
nori is an edible seaweed

explanation.surface: Someone urging action about a weed that keeps sprouting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer itself: I'm pressing, so I am one who irons.
explanation.definitionFit: One who presses clothes flat with an iron is an ironer.

clue.text: Quality of some cured meat from strain including American cattle

indicators.note: including puts one piece within the other

parts.note: stress is strain
A is the abbreviation for American
kine is an old plural of cow

explanation.surface: Bacon's quality traced to a breed of American cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaky bacon has alternating bands of fat and lean, and that striped nature is streakiness.

clue.text: Bit of foreign money in church one's invested

indicators.note: invested means clothed or wrapped, so the answer sits wrapped inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters run across the join between the two words

explanation.surface: A foreign coin someone has put into church funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested' looks financial, matching the money, but it signals the letters wrapped inside 'church one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The chon is a minor Korean currency unit, a hundredth of a won.

clue.text: Replace with another image gradually, mixed in Ford's case

indicators.note: mixed suggests the letters are stirred together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film-editing note about scenes in a John Ford picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' doubles as film and sound jargon, which hides its role as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To crossfade is to fade one picture or sound out while bringing the next in.

clue.text: Gill spreading wings, with full range to pick from (8, three words)

definitions.text: with full range to pick from

indicators.note: things spreading out on either side surround what lies between them

parts.note: alae is the plural of ala, a wing
in Chambers a gill is a two-wheeled cart for carrying timber

explanation.surface: A fish's gill opening, with a whole menu to choose from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gill' tempts as a fish organ or a liquid measure; here it is the timber cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering à la carte means choosing individual dishes from the whole menu rather than a set meal.

clue.text: Roll in mud say, a berth that's slippery and too hot initially?

indicators.note: something slippery will not stay put, so these letters slide into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words just before it

parts.note: the first letters of and, too and hot

explanation.surface: A muddy bunk that is slippery and far too warm for comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: An earth bath is a wallow in soil or mud, as animals or birds take; a mud roll is one example.

clue.text: Hubbub strangely odder when wife's involved — that hurts!

indicators.note: a thing involved is wrapped up inside something else
strangely suggests the word is behaving oddly, so its letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A row gets stranger once the wife joins in, ending in a yelp.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdedow is a noisy disturbance or uproar, a jocular old word built on row.

clue.text: Horse and colt in decline

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to sag is to sink or decline
C is the abbreviation Chambers gives for colt

explanation.surface: A horse and its young both going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' looks like the animal beside the colt, but it is slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Both horse and scag are slang names for heroin.

clue.text: One with vision unbroken, nerveless in part

indicators.note: in part says only a portion of the words before it is used

parts.note: the letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A seer who remains intact yet partly lacks nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A kenner is one who kens, that is knows or perceives, so someone with insight.

clue.text: Member of the family, good as dance partner?

parts.note: a son is a family member
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A relative who makes a good partner for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance partner' suggests a person, but it is the word paired with dance in the phrase song and dance.
explanation.definitionFit: In the stock phrase song and dance the two words always go together, so one is the other's partner.

clue.text: Pet having a suitable doctor brought in clipped as a proviso

indicators.note: something brought in is placed inside another thing

parts.note: a cat is a common pet

indicators.note: something clipped has had its end trimmed off

parts.note: a vet is the right doctor for a pet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pet taken to the right doctor for a trim, with a condition attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipped' reads as the pet's grooming but trims the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a warning or condition attached to a statement, which is what a proviso is.

clue.text: Finger food primate dipped in preserves

indicators.note: something dipped in is sunk inside the other thing

parts.note: to can is to preserve, so cans means preserves as a verb
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey dunking its fingers into jars of jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserves' looks like a noun for jam; it is the verb, to can.
explanation.definitionFit: Canapés are small savoury snacks eaten by hand at parties.

clue.text: What drains body cavity rips aorta in bits

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gruesome surgical scene in which a main artery is torn apart.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirator is a suction device used in surgery to draw fluid from the body.

clue.text: Holy scriptures: version thereof is Roman one

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
est is Latin for is, so a Roman way of saying it
a means one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Thereof' ties the surface to the scriptures but is padding in the wordplay.

clue.text: Napkins to twist up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry up means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to slew is to swing or twist round

explanation.surface: An instruction to roll napkins into a twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Napkins are small cloths for wiping hands and mouth, so a kind of towel.

clue.text: Acute anaemia, not universal in expressionist style

indicators.note: not says the following item is left out

parts.note: the bold-coloured early modern art movement of Matisse and Derain
U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: A medical condition oddly linked to a style of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Favism is a sudden destruction of red blood cells, a form of anaemia set off by eating broad beans.

clue.text: Paddy, soaked, succeeded coming first

indicators.note: coming first says this letter stands at the very front of the word

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded
awash means flooded or soaked

explanation.surface: A drenched paddy field that still did well.
explanation.walkthrough: The S already in AWASH is the one meant: it leaves its place and moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawah is a flooded field for growing rice in Indonesia and Malaysia, which is a rice paddy.

clue.text: Old snake may be in this cage

definitions.note: an obsolete sense of the answer

parts.note: an ingrate, an ungrateful person, is a snake in the old, dated wording
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cage that might once have held a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: The old snake may be IN followed by this word: take IN from the front of INGRATE and the rest is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grate once meant a grating or barred enclosure, so a cage.

clue.text: Wife after bit of coupling in bordello

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of coupling
a rib is a jocular word for a wife, from Eve made from Adam's rib

explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the order: the wife comes after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Crib is an old slang word for a brothel, as well as for a house or lodging.

clue.text: Alms required endlessly — see the old assemble

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: relief is help given to the poor

explanation.walkthrough: 'See the old' marks an archaic word, as a dictionary cross-reference would.
explanation.definitionFit: Relie is a Spenserian form of rally, meaning to gather together.

clue.text: Simon's chance encounter I'll abandon for possible primate once

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Simple Simon met a pieman
taken as written

clue.text: Farmstead flourished — as fed with this salt beef?

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

parts.note: C is the abbreviation Chambers gives for colt
taken as written
a pellet is a small pill

clue.text: Time to visit theatre bar? Poet's even taking in leaflet

clue.text: Churchman abandoning work, a mistake

parts.note: a bishop is a senior cleric

clue.text: Hated being confused, losing the point? What you'll find in the gods

definitions.text: What you'll find in the gods

indicators.note: being confused means mixed up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
the suffix -less means lacking
a ness is a headland or point

explanation.walkthrough: 'The gods' suggests the top gallery of a theatre; here it is the immortals themselves.
